newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Mirror reinvesting newsprint savings.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Mirror reinvesting newsprint savings.

text.p: Mirror Group Plc is seeing a 20 percent reduction in its newsprint bill but is ploughing some of the money saved back into its titles, chief executive David Montgomery said on Thursday.
"We are trying to enhance our papers rather than cutting the cover price," Montgomery said in a telephone interview.
"All the main newspaper groups are heavily subsidising cover prices in one way or another at the moment... We do not think this is the way to build a business," he added.
Montgomery said that Mirror Group spent in excess of 130 million pounds on newsprint last year.
The group has invested heavily on a revamp of its flagship Mirror national daily and Montgomery said that the benefits of that were beginning to feed through.
"We have clearly removed any (circulation) decline after last year's cover price rise and are now seeing some increases on last autumn," he added.
The Mirror, formerly known as The Daily Mirror, had average circulation of 2.395 million copies in February, a slight decline on the previous month.
Montgomery said that the Mirror Group had no plans to sell its 46.4 percent stake in Newspaper Publishing, which publishes the Independent and Independent on Sunday.
"These brands are strengthening all the time. They have an elite, young metropolitan market," he added, saying that advertising revenues were showing 10 percent growth.

There were signs last month that the two newspapers had halted their circulation slump. Sales of the Independent rose some 1.5 percent month-on-month to 257,000 in February, while the Independent on Sunday added 3.4 percent to 282,000.

Montogomery said operating losses at Newspaper Publishing had been cut by 43 percent in 1996 and said that cost savings from combined operations meant that the effect on Mirror Group was "negligible".
Montgomery denied that Mirror planned to bid for Midland Independent Newspapers, publishers of regional newspapers including the Birmingham Post.
"These rumours take root but there's no substance in them," Montgomery said.
Mirror Television, the unit which runs the Live TV cable channels, reduced its losses from 10 million pounds to around eight million.
The Broadcasting Act passed last year prevents Mirror from owning an ITV station but the Labour party has indicated it will review the rules if it wins the election.
"It would be nice to be liberated but an ITV company is not particularly a priority," Montgomery said.
